thread.title: Stocks Try To Hold Gains; Trump Sees Buy Opportunity | Investor's Business Daily

author: PAUL WHITFIELD
title: Stocks Try To Hold Gains; Trump Sees Buy Opportunity | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Bulls were looking to gain some conviction in the stock market Wednesday morning as the indexes surged at the open, but then eased. Doubts remain because of recent negative reversals, so investors will be watching to see if the market can either protect or build on the early gains.
X The Nasdaq was up 0.7%, while the large cap S&P 500 held a 0.2% gain. Blue chips were off the pace as the Dow Jones industrial average was just under flat. All three indexes rose more than 1% at the open.
Volume is almost certain to be higher today due to Monday's half session.
Trump Sees Buy Opportunity President Trump calmed the market with remarks Christmas Day. Trump affirmed support in Treasury Secretary Steven Mnuchin, calling him a "very smart person," and said the Federal Reserve will "get it pretty soon," Bloomberg News reported .
Trump added that the stock market is providing "a tremendous opportunity to buy."
Meanwhile, Trump and the Democrats waited to see who would blink first over the government shutdown and proposed U.S. border wall.
Stocks looked to end some ugly streaks. Casey's General Stores ( CASY ) popped 1.5% as it tried to end a seven-session losing streak.
Apple ( AAPL ) stabbed 1% higher after dropping in six of the past seven sessions. Apple is 36% off its high with no entry in sight on the chart.
Canada-based gold miner Kirkland Lake Gold ( KL ) gapped up 1.5% in heavy volume. The stock is up 8% from a breakout past a 23.96 buy point.
Stock Indicators Two secondary indicators are striking bullish notes in the stock market. Distribution in the Nasdaq, S&P 500 and Dow all currently earn E grades. (Generally, follow-through days on E-grade distribution do well).
The put/call hit 1.48 and 1.21 in recent sessions, a level of fear which often is bullish for stocks.
Investors IntelligenceBulls vs. bears gauge is off for holiday. The next reading is Jan. 2.
Economic Data Redbook's weekly gauge of same-store retail sales increased 7.8% in the week ended Dec. 22 vs. the year-ago figure.
The S&P CoreLogic Case-Shiller home price index for October rose 0.4%, matching the Street's consensus estimate.
